To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the SIR-SIS model with a sub-optimal immunity has a backward bifurcation, (ii) the SIR model with a nonlinear incidence and a sub-optimal immune response has oscillatory solutions and a backward bifurcations and (iii) the SIS model with a nonlinear and a sub-optimum immunity has a Bogdanov-Taken bifurcation point.
the backward bifurcation can occur in both models.

(1) the existence of backward bifurcations in the SIR model depends on the shape of the function F(I); (2) the existence of a Bogdanov-Taken's bifurcation depends on the value of the reproduction number, R0; and (3) the existence of oscillations depends on the value R0.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of the following models: SIR-SIR, SI-SIR, SIRS-SIS and SIRS-SIS.
the study of the dynamical behaviour of a large family of nonlinear models of infectious diseases, including the SIS and the SIR frameworks.
the dynamics of two types of epidemiological models, one of which is a modification of the SIS model, and the other is a modification of a model which is a transition from the SIR to the SIS model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SIS framework, which is the simplest model of a recurrent epidemic, is not always appropriate for the description of recurrent epidemics.
the presence of sub-optimal immunity, together with the nonlinear force of infection, can lead to a rich variety of dynamics, which is absent in the SIR framework.
the SIS model is more stable than the SIR model; the SIS model can be more oscillatory than the SIR one, and the SIS model has a greater tendency for multiple bifurcations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of a sub-optimal immunity mechanism and nonlinear incidence rate in the models can generate a richer dynamical behavior.

we have shown that the introduction of a nonlinear incidence function in the SIS and SIR models, together with the introduction of a non-monotonic function of the immunity, can give rise to complex dynamical behaviour.
the sub-optimal immunity can cause a backward bifurcation and the nonlinear incidence can cause oscillations in the model dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for certain values of the parameters, the SIS model exhibits oscillations which the SIR model does not exhibit.
the sub-optimal immunity can lead to the emergence of backward bifurcations and Bogdanav-Takens points.
, in the presence of nonlinearities, backward bifurcations may occur for models that are known to be forward-bistable in their linearized form.
